Primary Sources, Gortyn

Fornara, 86 (selection of laws on women from the Gortynian Code). Panelists
would do better to read the entire code (which is only about 10 pages).  For
this, use Willett' edition;  R. F. Willetts (ed. & tr.) 
The law code of
Gortyn
(de Gruyter, 1967).  Pages 18-29 of Willetts' introduction deal with
the legal position of women at Gortyn;  much of this information is also
presented (perhaps more readably) by Sealey.  

Secondary Sources

J.  Redfield  "The women of Sparta" 
CJ
  73 (1978) 146-161. 

P. Cartledge "Spartan wives. Liberation or license?"  
CQ  
31 (1981)
84-105. 

D. M. MacDowell,  
Spartan Law  
[Scottish Classical Studies, 1]
(Edinburgh, 1986) 71-88.

R. Sealey   
Women and Law in Classical Greece
 (U. North Carolina Press,
1990) 12-36, 50-88.

Main Questions

	Panelists should assume that groundwork for the legal status of Athenian women
has been laid by the other panel.  Compare the legal position of women in
Sparta and in Gortyn, especially with reference to the following issues:
property ownership, marriage, inheritance, monogamy, adultery.
